chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Rifa'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a divorced woman when she menstruates, is the right of return upon her for her husband? He said: Yes, until she becomes pure, because in this report there is no indication that he has the right of return upon her until she becomes pure from the third menstruation. And if that is not in it, we interpret it to mean that he has the right of return upon her in the first or second menstruation.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a husband's right to return his divorced wife during her menstruation periods?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to clarify the precise moment a revocable divorce (Talaq al-Raj'i) becomes final, specifically addressing the ambiguity of the third menstruation. The Imam explains that while the husband retains the right of return (raj'ah) during the first and second periods, the textual evidence does not explicitly mandate retention until the third is complete, allowing for the interpretation that the divorce is finalized upon the third menstruation ends. This highlights the Shia scholarly method of deriving legal nuances from the specific wording of prophetic traditions regarding the iddah period.
